summaryBox.title: Reaction Rate Concepts
summaryBox.takeaway: Average rate is measured over a finite time interval Δt; Instantaneous rate is the derivative at a specific moment (dt ──► 0).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
REACTION RATE CONCEPTS
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
  AVERAGE RATE ($r_{\text{avg}}$)                         INSTANTANEOUS RATE ($r_{\text{inst}}$)
  Change in concentration over a finite time             Rate of change of concentration at a specific
  interval ($\Delta t$).                                  infinitesimal instant ($dt \to 0$).
  $$r_{\text{avg}} = -\frac{\Delta [A]}{\Delta t} = \frac{\Delta [B]}{\Delta t}$$  $$r_{\text{inst}} = -\frac{d[A]}{dt} = \frac{d[B]}{dt}$$
conceptBreakdown.content:
Chemical Kinetics is the branch of physical chemistry that evaluates reaction rates, factors influencing rates, and the microscopic step-by-step mechanisms of chemical transformations.

• **Average Rate ($r_{\text{avg}}$)**: Change in concentration over a finite time interval ($\Delta t$).
  $$r_{\text{avg}} = -\frac{\Delta [A]}{\Delta t} = +\frac{\Delta [B]}{\Delta t}$$
• **Instantaneous Rate ($r_{\text{inst}}$)**: Rate of change of concentration at a specific infinitesimal instant ($dt \to 0$).
  $$r_{\text{inst}} = -\frac{d[A]}{dt} = +\frac{d[B]}{dt}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.1 Stoichiometric Rate Equivalences
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.1 Stoichiometric Rate Equivalences
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
STOICHIOMETRIC RATE EQUIVALENCES

For a general chemical reaction:
  a A + b B ──► c C + d D

Rate of Reaction = -(1/a) d[A]/dt = -(1/b) d[B]/dt = +(1/c) d[C]/dt = +(1/d) d[D]/dt

• Rate of Disappearance of A = -d[A]/dt
• Rate of Disappearance of B = -d[B]/dt
• Rate of Appearance of C    = +d[C]/dt
• Rate of Appearance of D    = +d[D]/dt

Rate of Disappearance of A = a × (Overall Reaction Rate)
conceptBreakdown.content:
For a general chemical reaction:
$$a A + b B \longrightarrow c C + d D$$

The overall rate of reaction is defined by normalizing individual rates of disappearance or appearance by their respective stoichiometric coefficients:
$$\mathbf{\text{Rate of Reaction} = -\frac{1}{a} \frac{d[A]}{dt} = -\frac{1}{b} \frac{d[B]}{dt} = +\frac{1}{c} \frac{d[C]}{dt} = +\frac{1}{d} \frac{d[D]}{dt}}$$

- **Rates of Consumption vs. Production**:
  - Rate of Disappearance of $A = -\frac{d[A]}{dt}$
  - Rate of Disappearance of $B = -\frac{d[B]}{dt}$
  - Rate of Appearance of $C = +\frac{d[C]}{dt}$
  - Rate of Appearance of $D = +\frac{d[D]}{dt}$

$$\mathbf{\text{Rate of Disappearance of } A = a \times (\text{Overall Reaction Rate})}$$

quickRevision: Rate of disappearance of A = a × (Overall Reaction Rate).
Rate is always a positive scalar quantity.
